Group-level conjunction of a joint interactive task (Leading and Following vs Rest) involves social interaction between participant and experimenter; meets whole-brain group task criteria and is social in nature.
No manipulation or contrast of relationship closeness, bonding, or affiliative value in the conjunction; AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 not met.

The conjunction reflects general sensorimotor network for joint movement rather than explicit communicative signals (faces, prosody, directed gaze or explicit imitation); SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 not met.
The conjunction is a general movement-related map (Leading and Following) and does not specifically target self-referential processing, agency or self-judgements; PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 not met.

Joint action necessarily involves perceiving and responding to another person's actions (action observation/interaction); the conjunction includes parietal/IFG/IPL areas consistent with action observation and social interaction.
Conjunction of Leading and Following (followers-only subgroup) reflects interactive joint-action task at the group level and thus meets social processing inclusion.
No relationship-closeness or bonding manipulation in this analysis; AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 not met.

Analysis reflects general sensorimotor and action-related activations rather than explicit communicative signal processing such as faces/gaze/prosody or explicit mimicry contrasts; SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 not met.
Conjunction does not specifically isolate self-referential or agency processes; PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 not met.
Joint interaction requires perceiving another's actions; followers' conjunction includes regions consistent with action observation and interpersonal processing.
Whole-group Leading > Following contrast derives from an interactive joint-action task and reflects social interaction between participant and partner; meets whole-brain task inclusion.
Contrast isolates leading-related motor/agency processes and does not manipulate relationship closeness or affiliative value; AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 not met.

Leading > Following emphasizes self-initiation and motor planning rather than receipt/production of communicative signals (faces, prosody, directed gaze, explicit mimicry); SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 not met.
Leading > Following engages agency, self-initiation and self-oriented motor planning (SMA, CMA, PMC), meeting perception-self inclusion for agency/bodily self processes.

This contrast predominantly highlights self-initiated motor control rather than observation/inference about another's mental states or actions; PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1 not met for this specific contrast.

No manipulation of relationship closeness or affiliative value in leaders-only contrast; AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 not met.

Leaders-only Leading > Following shows regions linked to agency and self-initiated action (SMA, CMA, PMC), satisfying perception_self criteria.
Contrast is focused on leader-specific motor control rather than perceiving others' mental states or action observation; PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1 not met here.
Followers-only Leading > Following is derived from an interactive joint-action task and thus meets the social processing global/local inclusion.
No relationship-closeness or affiliative manipulation in this subgroup contrast; AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 not met.
This contrast (leaders>following within followers subgroup) emphasizes cognitive control/agency (DLPFC) rather than explicit communicative signal processing; SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 not met.
Even though limited, the Leading > Following effect in followers includes DLPFC related to self-initiation/action selection; meets perception_self inclusion for agency/self-oriented processing.
This specific contrast does not primarily target perceiving or reasoning about another's mental states or actions; PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1 not met.
Whole-group Following > Leading contrast comes from a joint interactive task and engages social/mentalizing networks; meets social processing inclusion.
No manipulation of affiliative value or relationship closeness in this contrast; AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 not met.

Group-level whole-brain task contrast (feedback onset: self>other) involves social interaction, reception of social feedback and self-/other-referential processing. Meets global inclusion (healthy adults, whole-brain task-evoked map) and local social processing criteria.

Contrast does not manipulate relationship closeness or affiliative value; the contrast varies self vs other feedback but does not vary bond/relationship. Missing local inclusion AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1.

Contrast is about receiving evaluative feedback in a social interaction rather than core communicative signals (faces, expressions, gaze, speech) or simple face viewing contrasts; local inclusion SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 is not met.
Contrast directly tests self-referential processing (feedback about self > feedback about other). Meets global inclusion and PERCEPTION_SELF_I1.
Contrast also involves processing information about another person (other-related feedback), engaging perception/representation of others. Meets global inclusion and PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1.
Whole-brain, group-level contrast (feedback onset: other>self) concerns reception of social feedback about another person; meets global inclusion and social processing criteria.
No manipulation of relationship closeness or affiliative value; missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1.
Contrast focuses on evaluative feedback about another person rather than basic communicative signals (faces/expressions/gaze/speech); SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 not clearly met.
This contrast is other>self (emphasizes processing of others); does not primarily index self-referential processing (PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 not applicable here).
Contrast isolates processing of other-related feedback (other>self), engaging representation/inference about another person; meets GLOBAL_I1, GLOBAL_I2 and PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1.
This is a group × condition interaction (culture × self/other). Global exclusion GLOBAL_E3 applies (contrasts between groups / group x condition interaction are excluded).
Excluded because this analysis is a group × condition interaction which falls under GLOBAL_E3 (group comparison / interaction excluded).
Excluded due to GLOBAL_E3 (group × condition interaction).

Whole-brain covariate analysis on the contrast feedback onset: self>other (behavioral correlation with updating) concerns social feedback processing and meets global inclusion criteria.

Trial-by-trial parametric modulation of feedback ratings (self>other) indexes social reward processing of self-related feedback in a social task; meets GLOBAL_I1 and GLOBAL_I2 and social processing inclusion.
Modulation concerns reward-related responses to feedback about the self; no explicit manipulation of relationship closeness or affiliative value as required by AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1.
This analysis focuses on evaluative/reward aspects of self-related feedback (parametric correlation with ratings) rather than basic communicative signal processing (SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 not met).
Parametric correlation with self-related feedback ratings indexes self-referential valuation/processing; meets GLOBAL_I1, GLOBAL_I2 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I1.

Contrast tests self-specific reward-related modulation (self>other); while other-related processing was modeled, the contrast isolates self-specific effects and thus PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1 is not the primary inclusion for this contrast.

Whole-brain trial-by-trial correlation with feedback discrepancies (self and other) indexes social comparison/feedback processing across self and other; meets GLOBAL_I1 and GLOBAL_I2 and social processing inclusion.

This contrast captures social comparison/mentalizing related to feedback discrepancies but does not manipulate relationship closeness or affiliative value specifically; AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 not met.
Analysis reflects comparison-related/mentalizing activity rather than core communicative signals (faces/expressions/gaze); SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 not primary here.
Feedback discrepancies were modeled for self and thus engage self-referential comparison and updating processes; meets GLOBAL_I1, GLOBAL_I2 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I1.
Feedback discrepancies for other trials engage mentalizing and representation of others (TPJ, STS, etc. reported); meets GLOBAL_I1, GLOBAL_I2 and PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1.
Whole-brain map of negative correlations with feedback discrepancies (self and other) still indexes social comparison/feedback processing and meets global inclusion and social processing criteria.
No manipulation of relationship closeness or affiliative value is present; AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 not met.
This analysis reflects comparison/mentalizing components rather than core communicative signal processing; SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 not the primary match.

Effect also encompasses other-related trials and mentalizing regions, indexing representations of others; meets GLOBAL_I1, GLOBAL_I2 and PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1.

The contrast contrasts angry versus happy facial expressions in approaching characters (social stimuli). This is a social perception task and the contrast reflects social information (intentions/affiliation/dominance), meeting global and local inclusion criteria.

Although the authors interpret happy versus angry faces in terms of affiliation versus dominance, the contrast does not manipulate relationship closeness or attachment (no different partners/close vs. stranger or explicit bonding manipulation). Thus AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT inclusion is not clearly met (AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1/I2 not satisfied).
The contrast directly involves viewing and differentiating facial expressions and gaze (communicative social signals). This is a canonical social-communication task (face/emotion viewing).
This contrast does not engage self-referential processing or self versus other judgments; PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 is not met.

The task requires perceiving another person's emotional expression and inferring intentions (threat vs. affiliation), engaging perception/understanding of others and biological motion/intent inference.
The Happy > Angry contrast examines brain responses to social stimuli (faces and approach behavior) and thus meets global and local inclusion criteria for social processing.

Happy expressions in the paradigm explicitly signal affiliative intent (authors frame happy = friendly/affiliative), so the contrast varies affiliative value/relationship-relevant social signals and meets the affiliation inclusion criteria.
The contrast involves viewing facial expressions/gaze (communicative signals); simple face/emotion viewing qualifies under social communication.
No self-referential or self-versus-other processing is involved in this contrast; PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 is not met.

Although the task involves perceiving others, we limited assignment to two of the four specific constructs; perception-of-others is not separately labelled here. If stricter application were required, PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1 would apply, but it is not selected to keep labels within the two-construct limit.

Stories > Rest is a group-level whole-brain contrast of a task that presents social scenarios (social contracts, precautions, descriptives). The contrast reflects social-task processing (reading and interpreting social rules) versus baseline.
The contrast does not manipulate or vary relationship closeness, bonding, or affiliative value; it simply contrasts story reading versus rest. Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1.
Stories involve reading social scenarios but do not present communicative signals (faces, prosody, gaze) or explicit communication manipulations. Missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1.
Contrast does not engage self-referential processing or self-versus-other judgments. Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1.

Stories evoke reasoning about other people's behavior/mental states; Stories > Rest produced temporo-parietal activations associated with representing others, so this contrast engages perception/understanding of others.

Rest > Stories reflects deactivations relative to the task and does not itself index processing of social stimuli; the contrast does not reflect an aspect of the social task per se. Missing SOCIAL_PROCESSING_ALL_I2.
No manipulation of relationship closeness or affiliative value in this contrast (rest > stories). Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1.
Contrast does not involve communicative signals or face/voice/prosody manipulations. Missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1.
Contrast does not index self-referential processing. Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1.
Rest > Stories reflects greater activity at rest (default-mode) rather than direct representation/reasoning about others in the task contrast; it does not satisfy PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1.

Cards > Rest is a whole-brain contrast of the card-decision phase of Wason tasks about people's behavior (social content). The contrast reflects social-task decision processes and thus meets social processing criteria.
Card decisions do not manipulate relationship closeness or bonding; they ask about violations generally. Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1.
No communicative signal (face, prosody, gaze) manipulation in card responses. Missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1.
Card responses do not require self-referential judgments or agency judgments. Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1.

Card responses require judging whether individuals violated rules (reasoning about others' actions/intentionality). The cards > rest contrast includes temporo-parietal activations and reflects representing others’ behavior, satisfying PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1.
Rest > Cards reports activity greater at rest than during card responses and does not itself index processing of the social task; thus it does not satisfy SOCIAL_PROCESSING_ALL_I2.
No relationship-closeness manipulation in this contrast. Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1.
Contrast does not involve communicative signals or face/voice/prosody. Missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1.
Contrast does not index self-referential processing. Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1.
Rest > Cards reflects default-mode or rest-related activity rather than an on-task representation of others; it does not meet PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1.

Stories: Social Contracts > Precautions is a whole-brain contrast directly probing social exchange (cheater detection) versus precautionary scenarios; it clearly indexes social processing of exchanges.
Contrast compares social contract interpretation to precaution interpretation but does not manipulate relationship closeness or affiliative bond; missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1.
Contrast concerns social-exchange reasoning rather than communicative signals; no direct communicative-signal manipulation. Missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1.
Contrast indexes reasoning about others (cheaters) rather than self-referential judgments. Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1.

This contrast specifically activated neural correlates of ToM (anterior and posterior temporal cortex, posterior cingulate) when interpreting social-exchange rules, reflecting representation/inference about others’ mental states.
Stories: Social Contracts > Descriptives contrasts social-exchange rule interpretation against descriptive social rules, indexing social-exchange processing specifically.
No manipulation of relationship closeness or bonding; the contrast isolates social-exchange vs descriptive rules. Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1.
No communicative-signal manipulation (faces, prosody, gaze). Missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1.
Contrast concerns inferring others’ desires/intentions (social exchange), not self-referential processing. Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1.

Social Contracts > Descriptives activated anterior temporal cortex bilaterally—areas associated with ToM and inferring others’ mental states—so this contrast engages perception/understanding of others.

Stories: Precautions > Social Contracts contrasts interpretation of precautionary (hazard) rules versus social-exchange rules; both are social-rule tasks and this contrast indexes social processing related to hazard detection.
No relationship-closeness or affiliative value manipulation in precaution vs social-contract interpretation. Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1.
No communicative-signal manipulation in these story contrasts. Missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1.
Contrast concerns processing hazards and others’ situations rather than self-referential judgments. Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1.

Although these are social-rule stories, Precautions > Social Contracts did not activate canonical ToM regions and the interpretation does not require inferring others' mental states in the same way; thus it does not meet PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1 for mental-state inference.
Stories: Precautions > Descriptives contrasts precautionary-rule interpretation against descriptive social rules; this reflects social/hazard processing relevant to social cognition.
No manipulation of affiliative closeness or relationship value in this contrast. Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1.
No communicative signal (face/gaze/voice) manipulation. Missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1.
Contrast does not index self-referential judgments. Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1.

Precautionary interpretation did not differentially engage canonical ToM/mentalizing regions; the contrast reflects hazard-processing and safety evaluation rather than representing others’ mental states. Missing PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1.

Cards: Precautions > Social Contracts contrasts decision-phase activations for precaution violation detection versus cheater-detection; both involve social decision about other people's behavior and thus index social processing in the card phase.
No manipulation of relationship closeness or affiliation in these card contrasts. Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1.
Card-phase contrasts do not involve communicative signals (faces, speech, gaze). Missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1.
Decision-phase card contrasts do not require self-referential processing. Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1.

Although the cards concern others' actions, the Precautions > Social Contracts card contrast did not differentially engage canonical mentalizing/ToM regions; it indexes hazard-related decision circuitry rather than explicit mental-state inference required by PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1.

Cards: Precautions > Descriptives contrasts card-decision activations for precaution violation detection versus descriptive-rule decisions; both concern people’s behavior and thus reflect social processing at decision stage.
No relationship-closeness or affiliative manipulation in the card-phase contrast. Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1.
No communicative-signal manipulations in card decisions. Missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1.
No self-referential processing in these card contrasts. Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1.

The precaution > descriptive card contrast activated pre/postcentral and other decision-related regions rather than canonical ToM areas, so it does not meet PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1 for explicit mental-state inference.

Stories: Descriptives > Precautions contrasts interpretation of descriptive social rules about people’s traits/behaviors versus precautionary rules; it reflects processing of social content and social judgments.
Contrast does not manipulate affiliative closeness or relationship value. Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1.
No communicative-signal manipulation in descriptive versus precaution story comparisons. Missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1.
Contrast does not index self-referential processing. Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1.

Descriptive social-rule stories (preferences, habits, traits) activated right parahippocampal/amygdala regions implicated in social reasoning about others; this contrast engages representation/judgment about other people.

Cards: Descriptives > Social Contracts contrasts decision-phase activations when evaluating descriptive-rule violations versus cheater-detection; both are judgments about others’ behavior and thus reflect social processing at decision stage.
No affiliation/closeness manipulation in these card comparisons. Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1.
No communicative-signal manipulation in card-phase descriptives versus social-contracts. Missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1.

Cards: Descriptives > Precautions contrasts decision-stage activations for descriptive-rule evaluation versus precaution detection; both involve judging other people's behaviors and thus reflect social processing.
No manipulation of affiliative closeness or relationship value in this contrast. Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1.
No communicative-signal manipulation in the card contrasts. Missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1.
No self-referential processing required in these card comparisons. Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1.
